item.title: Critical Care Management of Disaster-Related Organ Failure.
item.description: Disasters generate high volumes of multisystem trauma while simultaneously degrading the staff, equipment, and electricity that critical care depends on. This article reviews management of disaster-related organ failure under resource constraint. item.title: Resuscitation of the Trauma Patient.
item.description: This article provides a practical overview of modern trauma resuscitation for emergency clinicians. It emphasizes early recognition of shock, timely hemorrhage control, and activation of massive transfusion protocols. Guidance is provided on fluid resuscitation, permissive hypotension, airway management, and treatment of agitation in critically ill trauma patients. item.description: Literature on the quality of death and dying has predominantly drawn on high-income contexts, while much less is known about end-of-life care in low-middle-income settings. In Vietnam, policy and practice around palliative and end-of-life care has not kept pace with the ageing of the population. item.description: Sepsis is a major global health challenge and increasingly affects patients with complex conditions such as malignancy. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to clarify endpoint-specific prognostic associations between malignancy and mortality in adults with sepsis or septic shock. item.title: Management of Patients After Cardiac Arrest.
item.description: This review outlines the acute management priorities for survivors of cardiac arrest, emphasizing organ support, hemodynamic stability, and investigation of the arrest cause. It highlights key areas of uncertainty, including targeted temperature management, neuroprognostication, coronary evaluation, and hemodynamic targets.

item.title: Intensive Care Unit Management of the Hemodynamically Significant Pulmonary Embolism.
item.description: This article reviews ICU management of hemodynamically significant pulmonary embolism. It highlights that patients with right‑ventricular failure, hemodynamic instability, or cardiac arrest require advanced monitoring and intervention. Key points include rapid diagnosis, risk stratification, timely reperfusion, and tailored hemodynamic and respiratory support.

item.description: Severe acute kidney injury in critically ill patients may require continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), yet mortality remains high. A standard CRRT intensity is 20-25 mL/kg/hr, because higher doses have not improved outcomes. item.description: Invasive fungal infections (IFIs) are challenging to treat in critical care, particularly among patients treated in Intensive care units (ICUs). item.title: Causal mediation analysis of contact with COVID-19 patients and burnout syndrome in physiotherapists in Japan: secondary analysis of a multicentre observational study.
item.description: This study looked at Japanese physiotherapists who worked with COVID-19 patients and found that direct contact with patients contributed to burnout, but this effect was partly buffered by appreciation and respect from patients and colleagues. The study suggests that organisational resources, such as reimbursement for care, may also play a role in burnout. Burnout prevalence was 19.4% among the physiotherapists.
